risk_flags.reason: Migration performs a table-swap on `documents`, a Parent-of-Sacred table that cascades into `questions` and through it `session_answers`. `DROP TABLE documents` (diff.patch line 22) with foreign keys enabled performs an implicit DELETE of all rows, firing ON DELETE CASCADE and destroying all child questions/session_answers — the exact pattern that wiped 790 questions and 746 answers on 2026-04-27. The migration was already executed (evidence/migration-output.txt), so loss may have already occurred.

Original `documents` table is dropped and replaced with `documents_new` that declares NO foreign keys; the swap runs outside any transaction and without PRAGMA foreign_key handling. Cascaded deletes of sacred tables are not recoverable from the migration itself.

DEC-U06 approves 'tighten documents schema — small, low-risk' in general terms; this is not an enumerated, specific pre-approval for a DROP/recreate table-swap on a Parent-of-Sacred table. Per sacred-data doctrine any new write path to documents is at minimum P1A absent specific enumeration.

The pack contains no schema definition or foreign-key listing for documents/questions/session_answers, so I cannot confirm whether cascades fired. Given the catastrophic stakes and the known-fatal pattern, this missing evidence compels escalation rather than a confident continue.

failure_classification.evidence: Failure history for this chunk records no prior failures; this is turn 1.

state_patch_proposal.objective: finish the 6-step upload pipeline build plan; step 6 (tighten documents schema) under P0 review for destructive cascade risk
state_patch_proposal.next_action: HALT — live human review of the documents table-swap migration; verify whether questions/session_answers survived and whether PITR recovery is needed before any further action

evidence.claim: Migration drops and recreates the documents table (table-swap) and recreates documents_new with no foreign-key declarations.
DROP TABLE documents is executed against the live DB; with FK enforcement this performs an implicit DELETE firing ON DELETE CASCADE into questions and session_answers.

Verification only compares COUNT(*) of documents before/after (22==22); it does not count questions or session_answers, so cascade-deleted sacred data would go undetected. Acceptance criterion 2 ('no data loss anywhere') is therefore not verified.
Migration was actually run, so any cascade damage may have already occurred.
Innocent-framing tell ('small, low-risk', 'tidy', 'close-out') attached to a destructive operation on a sacred-parent table.
